added_models.model: ADRB2 coding-variant genotype (Arg16Gly, Gln27Glu, Thr164Ile) as a predictor of trough-FEV1 response to vilanterol 25 ug, pooled across 17 COPD trials of UMEC/VI (GSK)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Pooled analysis of 17 trials run 2009-2013 with pharmacogenetic sampling; no single registry record, so registry_date is null. No earlier public record of ADRB2 genotyping for vilanterol: the Anoro NDA 203975 pharmacogenomics review (ClinPharmR section 4.2) covers CYP2D6 and umeclidinium PK only.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry: the genotype model was applied to a member drug and the comparison appears in the same paper, so first use and first comparison share the year (2016, epub April). Patient level: the question is whether ADRB2 genotype picks vilanterol responders, not whether the class works.
efficacy.model: ADRB2 coding-variant genotype (Arg16Gly, Gln27Glu, Thr164Ile) as a predictor of trough-FEV1 response to vilanterol 25 ug, pooled across 17 COPD trials of UMEC/VI (GSK)
efficacy.note: ADRB2 Arg16Gly, Gln27Glu and Thr164Ile genotyped across 17 UMEC/VI COPD trials as candidate selectors of vilanterol trough-FEV1 responders; comparison in the same paper.
efficacy.short: ADRB2 genotype tried as vilanterol selector
efficacy.quote: We investigated genetic association with treatment response to umeclidinium (UMEC, a LAMA), vilanterol (VI, a LABA), and combination therapy.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled); the three ADRB2 variants and the 1795 vilanterol-monotherapy patients are stated in the abstract, the per-variant effect sizes are not. Magnitude is null because the prediction was a difference by genotype and none was found; no ratio applies.
efficacy.reason: ADRB2 genotype did not pick responders
efficacy.judgement: Scored contra, following the glaucoma ROCK precedent: a patient-level genetic model exists to pick responders, the paper tests it against the trial primary endpoint (comparison_stated) and it picked nobody, so the model's prediction (differential vilanterol response by ADRB2 genotype, the hypothesis behind testing variants 'with prior evidence of associations') did not hold. The rules do not define the prediction of a pharmacogenetic analysis (checker rule question 5): read as the sponsor's null hypothesis, or as the LABA literature's null after LARGE 2009, this would be same. Class efficacy is unaffected; the track only says the genotype does not stratify.
efficacy.model: ADRB2 coding-variant genotype (Arg16Gly, Gln27Glu, Thr164Ile) as a predictor of trough-FEV1 response to vilanterol 25 ug, pooled across 17 COPD trials of UMEC/VI (GSK)
efficacy.note: In 1795 vilanterol-treated COPD patients (6075 pooled) no ADRB2 variant, HLA allele or GWAS SNP was associated with trough-FEV1 response: the genotype picked nobody.
efficacy.short: ADRB2 genotype did not predict response
efficacy.quote: None of the ADRB2 variants, HLA alleles or GWAS variants tested were associated with treatment response or baseline endpoints.

added_models.model: AstraZeneca semi-physiological compartmental lung-PK model (rat to dog to human) normalised by guinea-pig histamine-challenge lung IC50, linking predicted human lung concentration to COPD trough FEV1 for 12 inhaled bronchodilators including AZD3199

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text and supplement read (PMC5869554). AZD3199 is in Tables 1-2 (rat i.v./i.t. 1,000/15.7 ug/kg; guinea-pig total lung IC50 895 nM) and in Supplementary Table S5. Online 2017-12-27, print March 2018. AZD3199 was never filed, so model_filed is null.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first public use. The model was built after AZD3199's COPD data (Kuna 2013, NCT00929708 results posted 2014-01-17) were public, so its only comparison is a retrodiction, entered next.
efficacy.model: AstraZeneca semi-physiological compartmental lung-PK model (rat to dog to human) normalised by guinea-pig histamine-challenge lung IC50, linking predicted human lung concentration to COPD trough FEV1 for 12 inhaled bronchodilators including AZD3199
efficacy.note: AstraZeneca rat-to-human compartmental lung-PK model with guinea-pig lung IC50 built for 12 inhaled drugs including AZD3199; comparison with COPD FEV1 in the same paper.
efficacy.quote: Finally, the ability of using the model to predict human plasma profiles for 12 inhaled drugs (primarily bronchodilators) and explore their pulmonary PK/PD relationships was investigated.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: placebo-corrected trough FEV1 versus predicted trough lung concentration / guinea-pig lung IC50, class Emax fit; the AZD3199 residual is not reported
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text and Supplementary Table S5 read. AZD3199 contributes three points (200/400/800 ug od, day 28: 99/110/97 mL at ratios 0.41/0.82/1.6) to a beta-agonist class fit; the paper reports the correlation, not a per-drug fold error, so magnitude is direction only. Member drug AZD3199 only; vilanterol, abediterol and PF-00610355 are not modelled (PF-00610355 is named once in Table S5 beside Nielsen 2012, not verified as a data row).
efficacy.reason: Reproduces known AZD3199 FEV1; no prospective call
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the COPD trough-FEV1 data it correlates with were published (Kuna 2013, NCT00929708 results 2014-01-17) before the model, and the normalisation and Emax fits were made on them, so retro, never same. Class level: it rationalises AZD3199's flat 200-800 ug dose-response (all three doses at or above the beta-agonist half-maximal ratio) but made no prospective prediction for any member drug. Dose cell not opened: the same correlation would be counted twice; the paper's dose claim is a proposal for future drugs.
efficacy.model: AstraZeneca semi-physiological compartmental lung-PK model (rat to dog to human) normalised by guinea-pig histamine-challenge lung IC50, linking predicted human lung concentration to COPD trough FEV1 for 12 inhaled bronchodilators including AZD3199
efficacy.note: Built on published COPD data: AZD3199 200-800 ug (Kuna 2013) trough FEV1 97-110 mL at predicted lung 0.41-1.6x guinea-pig IC50 fit the beta-agonist curve.
efficacy.short: Lung-PK model refits AZD3199 trough FEV1
efficacy.quote: The model is shown to allow translation between animal species and predicts drug concentrations in human lungs that correlate with the forced expiratory volume for different classes of bronchodilators.

considered_not_added: Aparici 2016 (Eur J Pharmacol, doi:10.1016/j.ejphar.2015.11.053, PMID 26656755, epub 2015-12-04): dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety index (abediterol 10.5, olodaterol 4.9, vilanterol 2.4) and guinea-pig bronchoprotective t1/2 (vilanterol 18 h): the same Almirall guinea-pig/dog system as track almirall-guinea-pig-dog-bronchoprotection-heart-rate, run on vilanterol after its 2013 approval. Belongs on that existing track as a retrodiction safety entry (vilanterol's human dose-dependent heart-rate rise was already on the Breo label), not a new system.

Bjermer 2013 (Ther Adv Respir Dis, PMID 23907810, NCT00736489 results 2014-04-03): AZD3199 potassium/heart-rate/QTc versus formoterol in asthma: the patient side of the existing AZ guinea-pig track (checker correction, safety 6); no new system.
Hughes 2015 (Drug Des Devel Ther, PMID 25709399): AZD3199 systemic availability lower in COPD than in healthy volunteers: supports the existing AZ track's dose entry; no new system.

Nielsen 2012 longitudinal K-PD FEV1 model for PF-00610355 (doi:10.1007/s10928-012-9274-0): an in-silico model, but descriptive (fitted to the 690-patient COPD data it reports) and already the patient side of the Pfizer track; its one prospective output, the 100-200 ug nominal Phase 3 dose, was never tested because no Phase 3 ran, so no comparison exists.

Diderichsen 2013 heart-rate PK/PD model for PF-00610355 (doi:10.1111/bcp.12080): population model fitted to the 579-subject data it reports, already the patient side of the Pfizer safety track; no prospective prediction compared.

FDA Anoro NDA 203975 Pharmacogenomics Review (ClinPharmR section 4.2): CYP2D6 phenotype versus umeclidinium exposure only; nothing on ADRB2 or vilanterol, so no earlier regulator record of the genotype track and model_filed false for it.

FF/UMEC/VI population-PK models in COPD and asthma (Clin Pharmacokinet 2020, 2021; J Clin Pharmacol 2018): descriptive popPK of patient data with no preclinical-to-clinical prediction and no efficacy comparison.

Human isolated bronchi for vilanterol (Slack 2013) and later human airway smooth-muscle or BEAS-2B cell work with vilanterol (JPET 2024, Respir Res 2025): the bronchus work is already inside the GSK track; the cell papers carry no patient comparison.

Patient-derived organoids, precision-cut lung slices, ex-vivo drug sensitivity, human challenge (methacholine/allergen) for any member drug in COPD: none found in the Europe PMC sweeps; abediterol's asthma bronchodilation (Singh 2014, PMID 25398689) is a patient trial, not a challenge model.
Program-stop records (NCT04199598 abediterol termination 2020 for business prioritisation; PF-00610355 and AZD3199 stops): registry/business records, not model systems; nothing to add here.

Checker attribution note: doi:10.1002/psp4.12270 is Hendrickx, Lamm Bergstrom, Janzen, Friden, Eriksson, Grime and Ferguson (CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2018), not 'Boger & Friden 2018'; cited under the resolved authorship.
